note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

unit.title: Perform advanced welding using oxyacetylene welding process (OAW)

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A large nozzle needs more acetylene per hour than one cylinder can safely give. What should the job plan include?
options: Open the cylinder valve all the way to give a bigger flow
Lay the cylinder on its side so that more gas can come out of it at once
Two or more cylinders joined on a manifold, as the supplier advises
Warm the cylinder with the torch to raise the pressure inside

questions.stem: Why must acetylene not be drawn from a cylinder faster than the supplier's limit?
options: Acetone comes out with the gas and spoils the flame
The oxygen cylinder will empty before the acetylene one
The hose will swell and burst at the torch end
The regulator gauge will stop reading correctly

questions.stem: A heating nozzle uses about 1 200 litres of acetylene per hour. The supplier says one cylinder can safely give about 800 litres per hour. What is the least number of cylinders that must be joined on a manifold?
Why is oxy-acetylene often chosen to weld small-bore pipe on a farm in rural Clarendon with no power?
options: It always gives a stronger weld than any arc process
It needs no protective equipment for the welder or the people nearby
It welds faster than arc welding on thick pipe
It needs no electricity, and the set is easy to carry

questions.stem: How are flashback arrestors looked after in a well-run workshop?
options: Taken apart and oiled each week so the valve moves freely
Tested as the maker says, and replaced after any flashback
Never checked at all, as they are made to last for life
Tapped with a hammer each morning to free the valve inside

questions.stem: A crew must gas weld inside a large steel vessel. Why are the gas cylinders kept outside the vessel?
options: So the cylinders stay cooler in the shade outside
So the hoses are long enough to reach the work
So any leak cannot fill the space with fuel gas or extra oxygen
So the welder has more room to move about inside

questions.stem: An acetylene cylinder valve is leaking and will not seal when closed. What should the team leader do first?
options: If safe, move it outdoors away from flames, and call the supplier
Tighten the valve hard with a large wrench until it stops
Wrap the valve in tape and keep using the cylinder
Light the leak so that the escaping gas burns away in a controlled way

questions.stem: An acetylene cylinder becomes hot after a flashback reached it. What is the right action?
options: Carry it outside quickly so that it can cool down in the breeze
Open the valve fully to let the heat out with the gas
Keep using it until it is empty, then send it back to the gas supplier
Clear the area, call the fire service, and cool it with water from cover

questions.stem: A welder must gas weld a galvanised steel stand for a water tank. What is the special health risk?
options: The zinc makes the flame burn much hotter than usual
Zinc fume, which can cause metal fume fever
The zinc makes the steel give off acetylene gas
The coating makes the steel spark when heated

questions.stem: What is the main difference between a single-stage and a two-stage regulator?
options: A two-stage regulator can be used for oxygen and for acetylene alike
A single-stage regulator needs no gauges at all
A two-stage gives a steadier pressure as the cylinder empties
A single-stage regulator is fitted at the torch end

questions.stem: Most of the Centre's torches are equal-pressure (balanced) torches. What does this mean?
options: Both gases are fed at about the same pressure and mixed in the torch
The torch is the same weight at both ends, so it balances well in the hand
The two cylinders must hold exactly the same amount of gas
The torch can only be used with nozzles of one size

questions.stem: Why is a larger nozzle used for 8 mm steel instead of turning up the pressure on a small nozzle?
options: A small nozzle cannot be lit safely at all once the pressure is turned up
Higher pressure would empty both of the cylinders within a few minutes
A larger nozzle uses less gas than a small one
High pressure on a small nozzle gives a harsh flame that blows the pool

questions.stem: Which flame setting is normally used for gas welding aluminium?
options: A strongly oxidising flame
A neutral or very slightly carburising flame
A flame with no inner cone
A pure acetylene flame with no oxygen

questions.stem: Why is a carburising (excess acetylene) flame used when hardfacing with a cobalt-chromium type rod?
options: It lets the surface 'sweat', so the alloy wets it without deep melting
It burns away part of the hard alloy so it spreads out more thinly and evenly
It gives the deepest penetration into the base metal
It adds oxygen to the surface to make it harder

questions.stem: Why is a flux needed when braze welding steel with a bronze (brass) rod?
options: To make the bronze rod melt at a higher temperature than the steel itself
To make the finished joint shine without polishing
To dissolve oxides so the bronze can wet and bond to the steel
To cool the steel quickly so it does not distort

questions.stem: Why is it dangerous to leave aluminium gas welding flux on the job after welding?
options: It can catch fire when the job is painted later
It makes the weld too hard to file or drill
It gives off acetylene when it gets warm in the sun
It attracts moisture and corrodes the aluminium

questions.stem: In rightward (backhand) welding of thick steel plate, where is the filler rod held?
options: In front of the flame, ahead of the weld pool
Behind the flame, over the weld just made
Under the plate, on the back of the joint
Beside the joint, never touching the pool

questions.stem: Why is the leftward method a poor choice for steel thicker than about 5 mm?
options: It needs a wide joint angle, so it uses more rod and gas and fuses the root poorly
It cannot be used with a neutral flame on steel of that thickness or more
It makes the filler rod melt before the plate does
It can only be done in the overhead position

questions.stem: When gas welding a horizontal (2G) butt joint in plate, why is the top plate often bevelled more than the bottom plate?
options: So the welder can see over the top of the joint
So less filler rod is needed for the root run
So the bottom edge forms a ledge that supports the pool
So the flame can point straight down into the gap

questions.stem: In the 2G pipe position (pipe axis upright), how does the weld run?
options: Straight up the side of the pipe
Downhill from the top to the bottom
Along the length of the pipe
Horizontally round the pipe

questions.stem: When a run round a pipe is finished, why is the end taken a little past the start (a tie-in)?
options: To fuse the start and finish fully, with no crater or gap
To use up the last part of the filler rod that is left in the welder's hand
To make the cap look higher at that point
To let the pipe cool before it is moved

questions.stem: A small pipe assembly can be turned while it is welded. Which position is used, and why?
options: 5G fixed, because it is the easiest position
1G rolled, so all the welding is done in the flat
6G at 45°, so the weld can be tested later
4G overhead, so the pool cannot run out

questions.stem: Before gas welding a cracked cast iron bracket, why is a small hole drilled at each end of the crack?
options: To let gas escape from inside the casting
To mark where the welder should start and finish the welding run
To stop the crack running further when it is heated
To fix the bracket to the bench for welding

questions.stem: Which filler is used to fusion weld grey cast iron with oxy-acetylene?
options: Copper-coated mild steel rod with no flux
Aluminium rod with an aluminium flux
Stainless steel rod with borax flux
Cast iron rod with a cast iron flux

questions.stem: In braze welding, how does the welder know the steel has reached the right heat (the 'tinning' heat)?
options: The steel starts to melt and run like a weld pool
The bronze flows and wets the surface in a thin film
The steel turns bright white and gives off sparks
The flux turns black and smokes heavily on the steel

questions.stem: Aluminium shows no colour before it melts. Which sign helps the welder judge it is nearly ready?
options: The surface starts to look wet and shiny
The surface turns a bright cherry red
The surface gives off a shower of sparks
The surface turns from grey to blue

questions.stem: Why is aluminium sheet often supported on a backing plate or firebrick when it is gas welded?
options: So the flux does not drip onto the floor
So the welder can rest the torch on it
To keep the sheet cool all the time so that it does not melt at all
It loses strength when hot and can collapse without warning

questions.stem: Why is braze welding often chosen to repair a cracked cast iron part instead of fusion welding?
options: The joint is always stronger than the cast iron
No cleaning of the casting is needed first
Less heat means less risk of cracking and distortion
It needs no flux and no filler rod

questions.stem: What is the main limit of a braze-welded joint in service?
options: It cannot be painted once it is finished
It loses strength if the part works at high temperature
It always fails if the part is ever moved or knocked after welding
It cannot be used on any steel at all

questions.stem: A gas-welded steel sheet panel has buckled slightly. Which method can be used to straighten it?
options: Careful flame straightening with small spot heats
Heating the whole sheet red hot, then quenching it
Hammering it cold on a sharp edge until flat
Welding another run on the opposite face

questions.stem: A nick-break test on a gas weld shows a bright grey break with small dark spots. What do the spots show?
options: The steel was too thick for the nozzle used
The weld was cooled too slowly after welding
The filler rod was copper coated as it should be
Gas holes or oxide trapped inside the weld

questions.stem: A face bend test on a gas-welded butt joint opens a crack along the edge of the weld. What does this usually mean?
options: The joint was welded too slowly
The cap was too smooth and flat
Lack of fusion at the edge of the joint
The test strip was cut too wide

questions.stem: Why are the cap and root of a bend test strip dressed flush before it is bent?
options: So the strip fits into a smaller vice
So the shape of the weld does not cause a false fail
So the welder's mark cannot be seen
So the strip weighs the same as all the other strips in the test

questions.stem: Which fault found on a gas-welded pipe joint is the most serious and must be rejected?
options: Slight ripple marks along the cap
A crack at the toe of the weld
A small colour change beside the weld
Light scale on the surface of the pipe

questions.stem: A gas weld on 3 mm steel is very high and narrow, with poor fusion at the edges. Which is the likely cause?
options: Too small a nozzle, or too much rod for the heat
Too large a nozzle with too slow a travel speed
A slightly oxidising flame used on the sheet
Tacks placed too close together on the joint

questions.stem: Burn-through keeps happening near the end of each run on thin sheet. What should the welder change?
options: Use a bigger nozzle near the end of the joint
Hold the inner cone right on the pool at the end
Slow down at the end to fill the joint fully
Flatten the flame angle and travel faster near the end

questions.stem: Why are nozzles cleaned with the correct tip cleaner and not with a drill bit or a piece of wire?
options: Tip cleaners are faster than any other method and save the welder time
A drill bit would make the nozzle magnetic
The wrong tool can enlarge or scar the hole and spoil the flame
Wire can only be used on oxygen nozzles

questions.stem: After the torch valves are closed, a regulator's working pressure keeps rising slowly (it 'creeps'). What should be done?
options: Turn it down again each time the needle rises
Take it out of use, tag it and have it repaired or replaced
Tap the gauge glass until the needle stops moving
Oil the adjusting screw so that it moves freely

questions.stem: How often should the Centre's gas welding outfits be inspected?
options: By the user before each use, and at set times by a competent person
Only when a fault or a flashback has already happened
Once when they are bought, and never again after that unless they leak
Only when the gas supplier comes to collect the cylinders

questions.stem: A trainee lights the torch with the acetylene pressure set far too high and gets a large, sooty, roaring flame. What is the best coaching?
options: Tell him to light it with more oxygen next time
Let him carry on, since the flame will settle down once it warms up
Tell him to point it at the floor until it is clean
Shut it down, then show him the chart pressures and lighting steps

questions.stem: Before a group starts a gas welding practical, what should the team leader check on every set?
options: Only that the cylinders are full enough to last the whole day's practical work
Only that each torch has a nozzle fitted to it
Arrestors, check valves, hoses, regulators, secured cylinders and a leak test
Only that the spark lighters are working

questions.stem: Why is a record kept of every inspection and repair of each gas welding outfit?
options: To show it is safe and to track faults over time
So the supplier can charge for each inspection
So the outfit can be sold at a better price
Because the gas supplier will not deliver without it

questions.stem: After a backfire and flashback in the workshop, what must the team leader's report include?
options: Only the name of the trainee who was using the torch at the time
Only the time the gas was turned off
A note that nobody was hurt, and nothing else
What happened, the cause, the equipment checked or replaced, and actions

questions.stem: A WPS for an oxy-acetylene pipe weld gives the nozzle size. A welder wants a bigger nozzle 'to go faster'. What should happen?
options: Let him use it, since working faster saves both time and money on the job
Follow the WPS; a change needs approval and may need a new trial
Let him use it on the root run only
Let him use it if he lowers the gas pressures

questions.stem: Why are full and empty gas cylinders stored apart and labelled?
options: Empty cylinders are more likely to explode
Full cylinders must be kept in the sun
So crews take full ones, not empties, and stock is easy to check
So the gases do not mix in the store

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: Braze welding rods are mostly an alloy of copper and zinc. What is the name of this alloy?
Name the white powder, a compound of boron, that is often used as a flux for braze welding steel.
A nozzle uses 250 litres of oxygen per hour. How many litres are used in 3.5 hours?
What is the name for opening a cylinder valve briefly and closing it again, before the regulator is fitted, to blow out any dust?
What is the name of the test where a weld is cut across, smoothed and etched so its shape and fusion can be seen?
A pure acetylene flame, with no oxygen added, gives off black flakes and smoke. What are the black flakes?
What is the name of the material that fills an acetylene cylinder and holds the acetone?
Cast iron contains a lot of which element, which makes it brittle?
A cylinder holds 6 000 litres of acetylene. The supplier's limit is one-seventh of the contents per hour. To the nearest litre, what is the most it should give per hour?
What is the name for a root on the inside of a pipe that has sunk back to leave a hollow?
A job needs 18 m of weld. A welder completes 1.2 m an hour. How many hours of welding is that?
What is the name of the part of the torch where the oxygen and acetylene are mixed?
What is the name of the joint made when a smaller pipe is welded onto the side of a main pipe?
What is the name of the heat-resistant block used to support work on a gas welding bench?
What is the name of the larger, pale blue part of the flame that surrounds the inner cone and shields the pool?

essays.stem: You lead a two-person team to gas weld a broken steel gate frame and some small pipe at a farm in St Elizabeth with no power. Describe how you would plan the gas supply, equipment, safety and transport for the job.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would visit or ask about the site and the work, so I know the steel thickness, pipe sizes, positions and how long the welding will take. From the nozzle chart I would work out the gas needed and take enough full cylinders, plus a little spare. I would pack a checked outfit: regulators, flashback arrestors, check valves, hoses, torch, nozzles, tip cleaners, spark lighter, filler rod, flux if needed, clamps, tools and PPE. The cylinders travel upright and strapped in a ventilated vehicle, with valves shut, regulators off and caps on. On site I would set the cylinders upright and secured on firm ground, away from the work, and leak test before lighting. I would clear dry grass and other things that burn, keep an extinguisher and water ready, and plan where we can get help in an emergency. Any galvanised parts need extra fume control.
markingPoints: Finds out the job details and works out the gas needed from the nozzle chart
Packs and checks a complete outfit with arrestors and check valves
Transports cylinders upright, secured, valves shut and caps on, in a ventilated vehicle
Sets up safely on site with a leak test; clears combustibles; extinguisher ready
Plans for emergencies and fume (for example galvanised parts)

essays.stem: Describe step by step how you would repair a cracked cast iron machine bracket by fusion welding with oxy-acetylene, from preparing the crack to cooling and checking.
essays.modelAnswer: I clean the bracket of oil, paint and dirt and find both ends of the crack, using dye penetrant if needed. I drill a small hole at each end to stop the crack running. The crack is ground or chipped into a V down to sound metal, leaving the edges clean. Because cast iron cracks easily with uneven heat, I preheat the whole casting slowly and evenly, in a furnace or with a heating torch, to the temperature the procedure gives. I weld with a neutral flame, a cast iron filler rod and cast iron flux, keeping the pool fluid and working the flux in to float out oxides. I keep the casting hot while welding. When finished, I reheat it evenly and let it cool very slowly, covered with dry sand, ash or an insulating blanket. When cold, I clean it and check the repair for cracks by eye and with dye penetrant.
markingPoints: Cleans, finds the crack ends and drills stop holes
Grinds out a V to sound metal
Slow, even preheat of the whole casting
Neutral flame, cast iron rod and flux, casting kept hot
Very slow, covered cooling, then a check for cracks

essays.stem: Explain how to braze weld two pieces of steel tube with a bronze rod, and when braze welding is a better choice than fusion welding.
essays.modelAnswer: I clean the joint to bright metal and fit it closely, often with a bevel on thicker tube so the bronze can fill it. I use a slightly oxidising flame, which helps to stop the zinc in the rod boiling off. The steel is heated to a dull red, the tinning heat, but it is not melted. I dip the hot rod in flux, or use a flux-coated rod, and touch it to the hot steel: when it is at the right heat, the bronze flows and wets the surface in a thin film. I then build up the joint, moving along steadily and keeping the steel at tinning heat. Braze welding is a better choice for cast iron, for galvanised steel (less damage to the coating), for joining unlike metals and for thin parts that would distort. It is not used where the part works hot or needs full steel strength. Zinc fume must be controlled with ventilation.
markingPoints: Cleans and fits the joint; bevel on thicker sections
Slightly oxidising flame; steel heated to tinning heat, not melted
Uses flux; bronze flows and wets the surface, then the joint is built up
Better for cast iron, galvanised, unlike metals, thin parts; not for hot service
Controls zinc fume with ventilation

essays.stem: Describe how to gas weld 3 mm aluminium sheet, including cleaning, flux, flame, technique and after-care.
essays.modelAnswer: I clean the sheet of oil with a solvent and remove the oxide with a stainless brush or abrasive kept for aluminium. The flux is mixed as the maker says and painted on both edges and on the filler rod. The sheet is supported on a backing plate or firebrick because it loses strength when hot and can collapse. I use a neutral or very slightly carburising flame from a suitable nozzle, and warm the area first because aluminium carries heat away quickly. Aluminium does not change colour, so I watch for the surface to look wet and shiny, then start the pool and add rod steadily with the leftward method, travelling faster as the sheet heats up. After welding, all the flux must be washed off with hot water and a brush, because it attracts moisture and corrodes the metal. The area must be ventilated, as the flux gives off fumes.
markingPoints: Degreases and removes oxide with a dedicated brush
Applies flux to the joint and rod; supports the sheet
Neutral or slightly carburising flame; warms the area first
Watches for a wet, shiny surface; leftward, travelling faster as it heats
Washes off all flux after welding; ventilation for flux fumes

essays.stem: Describe how you would gas weld a small-bore steel pipe butt joint in the 2G position (pipe axis upright), and how you would inspect it.
essays.modelAnswer: I prepare the pipe ends with the bevel the procedure gives, clean them to bright metal, and line them up straight with an even gap. I tack in three or four places, evenly spaced. The pipe is fixed with its axis upright, so the weld runs horizontally round it. I use a neutral flame and the right nozzle from the chart. Because the pool tends to sag towards the lower pipe, I point the flame slightly upward and keep the pool small, adding rod to the top edge so it fills without undercut. I move round the pipe, changing my body position, and stop and restart with a good overlap, finishing with a tie-in past the start. For inspection I check the weld by eye for even width, no undercut on the top edge, no sagging, and even penetration inside where it can be seen. A sample can be nick-broken or bent to check fusion.
markingPoints: Prepares, cleans, aligns and tacks evenly
Fixes the pipe upright; neutral flame and correct nozzle
Flame angled slightly up, small pool, rod added at the top edge
Good restarts and a tie-in past the start
Visual check for undercut and sag, plus a nick-break or bend test

essays.stem: Explain the rules for drawing acetylene from cylinders, when a manifold is needed, and how cylinders are handled after a flashback or fire.
essays.modelAnswer: Acetylene is dissolved in acetone inside a porous mass. If gas is drawn too fast, acetone is carried out with it, which spoils the flame and can damage the equipment. So gas must not be drawn faster than the supplier's limit, which is often given as a fraction of the contents per hour. The cylinder must also be used upright, so the acetone stays in. When a large nozzle or a heating torch needs more gas than one cylinder can give, two or more cylinders are joined on a proper manifold, with the right fittings and arrestors, as the supplier advises. After a flashback, the torch and cylinder valves are shut and the cylinder is checked for heat. If it is warm or hot, the area is cleared, the fire service is called, and the cylinder is cooled with water spray from a safe place. The supplier is told, and the equipment is checked before reuse.
markingPoints: Explains acetone being drawn out if gas is taken too fast
Keeps within the supplier's withdrawal limit; cylinder used upright
Uses a proper manifold for large flows, as the supplier advises
After a flashback: shut valves, check the cylinder for heat
Hot cylinder: clear area, call fire service, cool with water from cover; tell the supplier

essays.stem: As team leader, describe how you would test a batch of trainees' oxy-acetylene plate welds: cutting test strips, face and root bends, nick-breaks, and recording and reporting the results.
essays.modelAnswer: First each test piece is marked with the trainee's number and inspected by eye for size, profile, undercut and penetration, and the results are written down. Strips are then cut across the weld from the places the test procedure gives, avoiding the start and finish. The cap and root are dressed flush and the edges rounded so the shape of the weld does not cause a false result. For a face bend, the strip is bent with the face on the outside; for a root bend, with the root on the outside. A nick-break strip has a saw cut in each edge of the weld and is broken so the inside can be seen. I record any cracks or openings, their size, and any gas holes, oxide or lack of fusion. Each result is compared with the acceptance limits, and a short report lists each trainee, the tests, the results and any retraining needed.
markingPoints: Marks and visually inspects each piece first
Cuts strips from set places, avoiding starts and stops
Dresses cap and root flush before bending
Explains face bend, root bend and nick-break
Records results against acceptance limits and reports by trainee with any retraining

essays.stem: Explain why gas welding causes distortion, and describe how you would use flame straightening to correct a buckled sheet panel.
essays.modelAnswer: Gas welding heats a wide area slowly. The hot metal expands but is held by the cold metal around it, so it is squeezed and thickens. When it cools it shrinks, pulling the sheet out of shape. Flame straightening uses the same effect on purpose. First I find the high spots or the long side of the bend with a straight edge. Using a small nozzle and a neutral flame, I heat a small spot on the high point quickly to a dull red, without melting it. As the spot cools it shrinks and pulls the sheet back. I work from the edge of the buckle in towards the middle, one spot at a time, letting each cool, and can cool a spot with a damp cloth if the steel allows. I check often with the straight edge and stop when it is flat, because too much heat makes it worse. This is done only as the supervisor directs.
markingPoints: Explains expansion, restraint and shrinkage causing distortion
Finds high spots with a straight edge
Quick spot heats to dull red with a small neutral flame
Works in a planned order, cooling between spots, checking often
Does not overheat; done as the supervisor directs

essays.stem: Describe how hardfacing is applied with oxy-acetylene to a worn part such as a plough share, including the preparation and the flame setting, and why it is done.
essays.modelAnswer: Hardfacing puts a layer of hard, wear-resistant alloy on a part that rubs on soil, stone or other parts, so it lasts longer and costs less than a new part. First the part is cleaned to bright metal, and any cracked or very worn metal is ground off. The part may be preheated, as the rod maker says, to avoid cracking. A carburising flame (excess acetylene) is used, so the surface of the steel just 'sweats' without being deeply melted. The hardfacing rod is then melted onto the sweating surface, where it wets and spreads, and is built up in thin, even layers to the shape needed, without mixing much of the base metal into it. The part is cooled slowly as the maker says. The finished surface is checked for cracks and even thickness. A record is kept of the rod used and the area covered.
markingPoints: Explains why: wear resistance, longer life, lower cost
Cleans and removes damaged metal; preheats if the maker says
Carburising flame so the surface sweats without deep melting
Builds up thin, even layers with little mixing
Slow cooling, inspection and a record

essays.stem: Describe a regular inspection programme for the Centre's oxy-acetylene outfits: what is checked, how often, by whom, and what is recorded.
essays.modelAnswer: Each outfit gets a number. Before every use, the user checks the cylinders are upright and chained, the regulators and gauges are undamaged, the arrestors and check valves are fitted, the hoses are not cut, burnt or perished, the fittings are tight and free of oil, the torch and nozzle are clean, and a leak test is passed. Any fault is tagged out and reported. At set times, such as every month, a competent person does a fuller check: regulators for creep (the pressure rising when the torch is shut), arrestors tested or replaced as the maker says, hoses replaced if worn, and torches and valves inspected. Any outfit involved in a flashback is checked before it is used again. Every check and repair is written in a log for that outfit, with the date, the person, what was found and what was done, so faults can be tracked and the Centre can show its equipment is safe.
markingPoints: Each outfit numbered and checked by the user before every use
Lists the pre-use checks, including a leak test
Faulty items tagged out and reported
Periodic checks by a competent person, and after any flashback
Log of date, person, findings and actions for each outfit

practical1.title: Planned overhead (4G) and horizontal (2G) butt welds in 3 mm steel sheet, with face and root bend tests
practical1.brief: As a group, read the procedure the assessor gives and write a short job plan: the nozzle size from the maker's chart, the pressures, the filler rod, the joint gap and the order of work, with who does what. Set up and leak-test the outfits together and record the checks on an equipment checklist. Each member then welds one butt joint in 3 mm mild steel sheet in the horizontal position (2G) and one in the overhead position (4G), using the leftward method. While one member welds, another watches the flame setting and records it. When cool, the group inspects each joint by eye and records the results. Each member cuts strips from their joints by the method the Centre allows, dresses them flush, and the group bends one face bend and one root bend for each member and records the results. Photograph each stage and add the photos, the plan and the records to the group's practical.
materials: Oxy-acetylene outfits with flashback arrestors and check valves (two or more stations)
Nozzles to suit 3 mm steel from the maker's chart, tip cleaners and spark lighters
Pairs of 3 mm mild steel sheet, about 150 mm × 50 mm (two joints per member)
Positioners or clamps to hold work horizontal and overhead
Vice, files, grinder, tongs, and the plan, checklist and test record sheets
photos: The equipment checklist and the leak test being done
A joint fixed in the 2G position, with a member welding in PPE
A joint fixed overhead, with a member welding in PPE
Each member's finished 2G and 4G welds, face and back
Test strips dressed flush and marked
The bent strips, labelled face and root, for each member
The completed test record and the outfits shut down
checklist: Took part in the written plan and followed it
Helped check and leak-test the outfit and recorded it
Set a neutral flame with the right nozzle and pressures
Controlled the pool in 2G (no sag or top-edge undercut) and in 4G (no drips)
Even penetration on the back of each joint
Bend strips showed no cracks or openings beyond what the procedure allows
Recorded results accurately and shut the outfit down correctly
Wore suitable PPE throughout, with head and shoulder cover for overhead work
safety: Cylinders chained upright; leak-test with solution before lighting; follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
Keep oil and grease away from oxygen fittings
Wear a cap, collar and sleeves for overhead work: hot metal falls
Clear anything that burns and keep an extinguisher at hand
Never leave a lit torch; hang it up away from the cylinders when not in use
Treat test pieces as hot; use tongs and mark them HOT

practical2.title: Plan, weld and test a small-bore steel pipe assembly with 2G and 5G joints and a braze-welded branch
practical2.brief: As a group, plan a small pipe assembly from the sketch the assessor gives: a straight run with one butt joint welded in the 2G position (axis upright), one in the 5G position (axis horizontal and fixed), and one small branch braze welded onto the side. Write the plan: the cut list, edge preparation, nozzle and flame for each joint, filler and flux, the order of work and who does each joint. Every member must weld at least one butt joint, and the branch is braze welded by members in turn under the assessor's watch. A member acts as inspector for each joint, checking the fit-up and recording it. The group inspects the finished assembly and records the results. The assessor cuts one butt joint for a nick-break test, and the group records what the break shows. Finally the group writes a short job report: what was done, gas used, faults found and what they would change. Photograph each stage.
materials: Small-bore mild steel pipe (about 25 mm to 50 mm outside diameter) cut to the sketch, with spare pieces for each member
Oxy-acetylene outfits with arrestors and check valves; nozzles from the maker's chart
Copper-coated mild steel filler rod; bronze rod and braze welding flux
Pipe stands or clamps for 2G and 5G
Files, grinder, hacksaw, tongs, square and tape
The sketch, plan sheet, inspection record and job report form
photos: The group's written plan and cut list
The pipe ends prepared and tacked, with the gap shown
A member welding the 2G joint in PPE
A member welding the 5G joint in PPE
The finished assembly, with each joint labelled
The completed inspection record and job report
checklist: Took part in the plan and the cut list
Prepared, aligned and tacked a pipe joint correctly
Welded a butt joint with even fusion and a good tie-in
Used the right flame and technique for braze welding (or watched and recorded it)
Inspected and recorded results accurately as inspector
Nick-break showed sound fusion with few defects
Shut down the outfits and left the area clean and safe
safety: Cylinders upright and chained; leak-test before lighting
Braze welding gives zinc fume: work with extraction or good ventilation
Clear anything that burns; keep an extinguisher at hand
Hang up torches when not in use; never point a lit torch at people or cylinders
Treat pipes as hot; use tongs and mark them HOT
Only the assessor breaks the test piece; stand clear and wear eye protection
